### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, activity A01 did not occur in any trace; in the later window, it occurs in every trace, on average once per trace. [OCC001]
- In the earlier window, activity A06 had no observed outgoing transitions; in the later window, all outgoing transitions from A06 lead to A01. [DIR001]
- In the earlier window, A01 had no position; in the later window, it appears at a fixed position (mean 1.0). [POS001]
- In the earlier window, A06 appeared at a fixed position (mean 1.0) with no variation; in the later window, its position shifted slightly earlier (mean ~0.87) with some variation. [POS002]
- In the earlier window, A01 and A06 never co-occurred; all traces contained A06 only. In the later window, they co-occur in every trace, with A06 always before A01. [REL001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, a new activity A01 was added after A06, so that traces changed from consisting solely of A06 to consisting of A06 followed by A01. This is directly shown by the complete appearance of A01 (OCC001), the new outgoing edge from A06 to A01 (DIR001), the co-occurrence and fixed order A06 before A01 (REL001), and the positional shifts of both activities (POS001, POS002). The change is consistent across all five items, and the number of qualifying items (5) far exceeds the 0.04 expected by chance under a stable process. A competing explanation, such as a rare variant or sampling fluctuation, is effectively ruled out by the magnitude and consistency of the evidence.
